items.stem: State any three types of entrepreneurs according to Clarence Danhof.
items.answer: Innovative; Imitating (adoptive); Fabian; Drone
items.markingKey: Any three of: Innovative; Imitating (adoptive); Fabian; Drone (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Agri-entrepreneur" with reference to the other types of entrepreneurs.
items.answer: Agri-entrepreneur: Runs a venture in agriculture or allied activities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Runs a venture in agriculture or allied activities.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about types of entrepreneurs is NOT correct?
items.answer: An imitating entrepreneur invents completely new products.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: An imitating entrepreneur invents completely new products.
options: An innovative entrepreneur introduces new goods or methods.
A drone entrepreneur refuses to change.
An imitating entrepreneur invents completely new products.
Clarence Danhof classified entrepreneurs as innovative, imitating, Fabian and drone.

items.stem: Aarav started selling online only after his offline sales fell sharply. Which type of entrepreneur is this?
items.answer: Fabian entrepreneur
items.markingKey: (d) Fabian entrepreneur. Aarav adopted change only when forced.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Shreya started selling online only after her offline sales fell sharply. (a) Which type of entrepreneur is this? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Fabian entrepreneur (b) Shreya adopted change only when forced.
items.markingKey: (a) Fabian entrepreneur, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Shreya adopted change only when forced.

items.stem:
Four shopkeepers in Kochi: A started the town's first app-based grocery delivery; B copied it a year later; C began delivery only after losing half his customers; D still refuses to deliver even though his sales keep falling.
(i) Identify the type of entrepreneur each represents according to Danhof, with a reason. (ii) Which type is most useful in a developing economy and why?
items.answer: (i) A – innovative (first to introduce); B – imitating (copied a successful idea); C – Fabian (changed only when forced by losses); D – drone (refuses to change despite losses). (ii) Imitating, because they spread proven innovations quickly at lower risk.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) A – innovative (first to introduce); B – imitating (copied a successful idea); C – Fabian (changed only when forced by losses); D – drone (refuses to change despite losses). (ii) Imitating, because they spread proven innovations quickly at lower risk.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about types of entrepreneurs is correct?
items.answer: An innovative entrepreneur introduces new goods or methods.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: An innovative entrepreneur introduces new goods or methods.
options: A Fabian entrepreneur is always the first to try new ideas.
An imitating entrepreneur invents completely new products.
An innovative entrepreneur introduces new goods or methods.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "An entrepreneur who copies successful innovations made by others, often adapting them to local needs."
items.answer: Imitating entrepreneur
items.markingKey: (a) Imitating entrepreneur: An entrepreneur who copies successful innovations made by others, often adapting them to local needs.

items.stem:
Rohan and three other women of a self-help group in a village started making jute bags and selling them in nearby towns.
(i) Identify two types of entrepreneurs they represent. (ii) Give one feature of each.
items.answer: (i) Women entrepreneurs; rural entrepreneurs. (ii) Women entrepreneurs – enterprise started and run by women; rural – set up in a village using local resources.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Women entrepreneurs; rural entrepreneurs. (ii) Women entrepreneurs – enterprise started and run by women; rural – set up in a village using local resources.

items.stem: Lakshmi runs a venture that trains and employs visually impaired people to make candles. Which type of entrepreneur is this? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Social entrepreneur. The main aim is to solve a social problem.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Social entrepreneur; 2 marks for the justification: The main aim is to solve a social problem.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Persistence"?
items.answer: Continuing to work towards a goal despite obstacles.
items.markingKey: (c) Persistence: Continuing to work towards a goal despite obstacles.
options: Taking moderate risks after weighing the likely gains and losses.
Doing things before being asked or forced by events.
Continuing to work towards a goal despite obstacles.
Belief in one's own ability to complete a task or meet a challenge.

items.stem: Explain "Self-confidence" with reference to the competencies of an entrepreneur.
items.answer: Self-confidence: Believes in own ability to succeed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Believes in own ability to succeed.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Entrepreneurs usually take calculated risks.
Reason (R): They weigh gains and losses before deciding.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Nikhil divided his launch into weekly tasks with a deadline for each. Which competency is the entrepreneur showing?
items.answer: Systematic planning
items.markingKey: (d) Systematic planning. A large task was broken into planned steps.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Kavya rejects any batch of pickles that does not meet her strict taste standard. (a) Which competency is the entrepreneur showing? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Concern for high quality of work (b) Kavya insists on doing things better.
items.markingKey: (a) Concern for high quality of work, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Kavya insists on doing things better.

items.stem: Before launching her juice bar, Riya talked to 100 office workers about their drinks preferences. Which competency is the entrepreneur showing? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Information seeking. Information was gathered from potential customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Information seeking; 2 marks for the justification: Information was gathered from potential customers.

items.stem:
Before opening a cycle-repair and rental shop near a college in Varanasi, Aditya met students to learn what they needed, prepared a month-by-month plan, and convinced his uncle to invest. When the first location failed, he moved to a better site and kept going. He checks every repaired cycle personally.
(i) Identify five competencies shown by Aditya, quoting the lines.
items.answer: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).

items.stem:

items.answer: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about entrepreneurial competencies is correct?
items.answer: Entrepreneurs usually take moderate, calculated risks.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Entrepreneurs usually take moderate, calculated risks.
options: Entrepreneurs avoid all information from customers.
Entrepreneurs usually take moderate, calculated risks.
Entrepreneurs take only very high, blind risks.

items.stem: State one difference between competency and trait on the basis of development.
items.answer: competency: developed through training and practice; trait: changes slowly, if at all
items.markingKey: 1 mark: competency: developed through training and practice; trait: changes slowly, if at all

items.stem:
Harleen always sets difficult sales targets for her shop and likes regular feedback on how she is doing.
(i) Which motive is shown? (ii) Who linked it with entrepreneurship? (iii) Give one other trait of entrepreneurs.
items.answer: (i) Need for achievement. (ii) David McClelland. (iii) Self-confidence; calculated risk taking; initiative; persistence (any one).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Need for achievement. (ii) David McClelland. (iii) Self-confidence; calculated risk taking; initiative; persistence (any one).

items.stem: State any three entrepreneurial values and attitudes.
items.answer: Innovativeness and creativity; Independence; Respect for work; Openness to feedback and learning from failure; Ethical conduct
items.markingKey: Any three of: Innovativeness and creativity; Independence; Respect for work; Openness to feedback and learning from failure; Ethical conduct (1 mark each).

items.stem: State any three features of an intrapreneur.
items.answer: Works within an organisation; Innovative; Uses the organisation's resources; Limited risk; Driven by recognition and achievement
items.markingKey: Any three of: Works within an organisation; Innovative; Uses the organisation's resources; Limited risk; Driven by recognition and achievement (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Driven by recognition and achievement" with reference to the features of an intrapreneur.
items.answer: Driven by recognition and achievement: Rewards include bonuses, promotion and freedom to work on ideas.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Rewards include bonuses, promotion and freedom to work on ideas.

items.stem: Distinguish between entrepreneur and manager on the basis of risk, innovation and status.
items.answer: (i) Risk: entrepreneur: bears the risk and uncertainty; manager: does not bear the risk of ownership. (ii) Innovation: entrepreneur: introduces new ideas and changes; manager: carries out existing plans and policies. (iii) Status: entrepreneur: owner of the enterprise; manager: employee of the enterprise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Risk: entrepreneur: bears the risk and uncertainty; manager: does not bear the risk of ownership. (ii) Innovation: entrepreneur: introduces new ideas and changes; manager: carries out existing plans and policies. (iii) Status: entrepreneur: owner of the enterprise; manager: employee of the enterprise.

items.stem: A bank employee, Nikhil, designed a new mobile app for the bank's farmer customers and was given a team to build it. Who is this person?
items.answer: Intrapreneur
items.markingKey: (c) Intrapreneur. Nikhil innovated inside the organisation with its resources.

items.stem:
A software company lets its employees spend some of their working time on their own ideas for new products.
(i) What type of behaviour is the company encouraging? (ii) State two benefits to the company.
items.answer: (i) Intrapreneurship. (ii) New products and processes; keeps talented employees; stays competitive and innovative (any two).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Intrapreneurship. (ii) New products and processes; keeps talented employees; stays competitive and innovative (any two).

items.stem:
Sneha works at a large food company in Guwahati. She suggested a millet-based breakfast cereal, and the company gave her a budget and a team to develop it. Her friend Kabir left a similar job, borrowed money and started an independent snacks brand. A third friend supervises a factory for a fixed salary.
(i) Identify the role of each person. (ii) Distinguish between Sneha and Kabir on three bases.
items.answer: (i) Sneha – intrapreneur; Kabir – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Kabir; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Sneha – intrapreneur; Kabir – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Kabir; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).

items.stem: Sahil left his job, used his savings and started a company making eco-friendly plates. Who is this person? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Entrepreneur. Sahil owns the venture and bears the risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Entrepreneur; 2 marks for the justification: Sahil owns the venture and bears the risk.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. A bank employee, Aditi, designed a new mobile app for the bank's farmer customers and was given a team to build it. (a) Who is this person? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Intrapreneur (b) Aditi innovated inside the organisation with its resources.
items.markingKey: (a) Intrapreneur, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Aditi innovated inside the organisation with its resources.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of entrepreneur but not of intrapreneur?
items.answer: Reward: profit
items.markingKey: (c) entrepreneur: Reward: profit. The other options describe intrapreneur.
options: Funds: uses funds of the organisation

(i) Identify the role of each person. (ii) Distinguish between Ishaan and Meera on three bases.
items.answer: (i) Ishaan – intrapreneur; Meera – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Meera; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Ishaan – intrapreneur; Meera – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Meera; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Pull factors"?
items.answer: Attractive conditions, such as an opportunity, independence or high income, that draw a person into entrepreneurship.
items.markingKey: (b) Pull factors: Attractive conditions, such as an opportunity, independence or high income, that draw a person into entrepreneurship.
options: The inner drive that moves a person to act towards a goal.
Attractive conditions, such as an opportunity, independence or high income, that draw a person into entrepreneurship.
The obligation of a business to act for the benefit of society beyond earning profit.
Negative conditions, such as unemployment or job dissatisfaction, that force a person to start a business.

items.stem: Explain "Recognition and social status" with reference to the motivating factors for entrepreneurs.
items.answer: Recognition and social status: Respect gained from success.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Respect gained from success.

items.stem: Meera lost her factory job when the plant closed and started a tea stall to support the family. Is this a push factor or a pull factor?
items.answer: Push factor
items.markingKey: (b) Push factor. Unemployment forced Meera into business.

items.stem:
A shopkeeper in Pune sells fake branded shoes at full price.
(i) Which ethical principle is violated? (ii) Give two harms this can cause to the business.
items.answer: (i) Honesty with customers (no false claims). (ii) Loss of customer trust and reputation; legal action and penalties; loss of future sales (any two).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Honesty with customers (no false claims). (ii) Loss of customer trust and reputation; legal action and penalties; loss of future sales (any two).

items.stem:
Dev started a spice-packing business in Nagpur because he wanted independence. He pays fair wages, gives correct weights, files taxes on time and has stopped using plastic packets. A rival suggested that he mix cheaper powder to raise profits, but he refused.
(i) Is Dev's motivation a push or a pull factor? (ii) Identify four ethical practices followed by Dev.
items.answer: (i) Pull factor (desire for independence). (ii) Fair treatment of employees; honesty with customers; payment of taxes; protection of the environment; refusing adulteration (any four).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Pull factor (desire for independence). (ii) Fair treatment of employees; honesty with customers; payment of taxes; protection of the environment; refusing adulteration (any four).

Before opening a cycle-repair and rental shop near a college in Guwahati, Gauri met students to learn what they needed, prepared a month-by-month plan, and convinced her uncle to invest. When the first location failed, she moved to a better site and kept going. She checks every repaired cycle personally.
(i) Identify five competencies shown by Gauri, quoting the lines.
items.answer: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Information seeking (met students); systematic planning (month-by-month plan); persuasion (convinced uncle); persistence (kept going after failure); concern for high quality (checks every cycle).

items.stem: After seeing cloud kitchens succeed in Bengaluru, Ishaan opened one in his town. Which type of entrepreneur is this?
items.answer: Imitating entrepreneur
items.markingKey: (c) Imitating entrepreneur. Ishaan copied a successful idea.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A Fabian entrepreneur is very cautious.
Reason (R): A Fabian entrepreneur adopts change only when failure to do so would cause losses.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Om started a business because he was unhappy with his boss and the long hours in the office. Is this a push factor or a pull factor?
items.answer: Push factor
items.markingKey: (c) Push factor. Dissatisfaction with the job pushed Om out.

items.stem: Distinguish between entrepreneur and intrapreneur on the basis of funds, dependence and risk.
items.answer: (i) Funds: entrepreneur: raises funds personally; intrapreneur: uses funds of the organisation. (ii) Dependence: entrepreneur: independent, owns the venture; intrapreneur: works within an organisation. (iii) Risk: entrepreneur: bears the full risk; intrapreneur: the organisation bears most of the risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Funds: entrepreneur: raises funds personally; intrapreneur: uses funds of the organisation. (ii) Dependence: entrepreneur: independent, owns the venture; intrapreneur: works within an organisation. (iii) Risk: entrepreneur: bears the full risk; intrapreneur: the organisation bears most of the risk.

items.stem:
Zoya started a spice-packing business in Pune because she wanted independence. She pays fair wages, gives correct weights, files taxes on time and has stopped using plastic packets. A rival suggested that she mix cheaper powder to raise profits, but she refused.
(i) Is Zoya's motivation a push or a pull factor? (ii) Identify four ethical practices followed by Zoya.
items.answer: (i) Pull factor (desire for independence). (ii) Fair treatment of employees; honesty with customers; payment of taxes; protection of the environment; refusing adulteration (any four).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Pull factor (desire for independence). (ii) Fair treatment of employees; honesty with customers; payment of taxes; protection of the environment; refusing adulteration (any four).

items.stem: Zoya rejects any batch of pickles that does not meet her strict taste standard. Which competency is the entrepreneur showing?
items.answer: Concern for high quality of work
items.markingKey: (d) Concern for high quality of work. Zoya insists on doing things better.
options: Concern for high quality of work

items.stem: Differentiate between entrepreneur and intrapreneur with reference to funds and reward.
items.answer: (i) Funds: entrepreneur: raises funds personally; intrapreneur: uses funds of the organisation. (ii) Reward: entrepreneur: profit; intrapreneur: salary, bonus or recognition.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Funds: entrepreneur: raises funds personally; intrapreneur: uses funds of the organisation. (ii) Reward: entrepreneur: profit; intrapreneur: salary, bonus or recognition.

items.stem: Nikhil is employed to keep the accounts and the staff of a hotel running smoothly. Who is this person?
items.answer: Manager
items.markingKey: (d) Manager. Nikhil runs existing operations for a salary.

items.stem: Differentiate between innovative entrepreneur and imitating entrepreneur with reference to where common and risk.
items.answer: (i) Where common: innovative entrepreneur: more common in developed and fast-changing industries; imitating entrepreneur: more common in developing economies. (ii) Risk: innovative entrepreneur: high risk; imitating entrepreneur: lower risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Where common: innovative entrepreneur: more common in developed and fast-changing industries; imitating entrepreneur: more common in developing economies. (ii) Risk: innovative entrepreneur: high risk; imitating entrepreneur: lower risk.

items.stem: What is meant by "Need for achievement"?
items.answer: The desire to excel and accomplish challenging goals, which McClelland linked with entrepreneurship.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The desire to excel and accomplish challenging goals, which McClelland linked with entrepreneurship.

items.stem:
Mehak works at a large food company in Bhopal. She suggested a millet-based breakfast cereal, and the company gave her a budget and a team to develop it. Her friend Fatima left a similar job, borrowed money and started an independent snacks brand. A third friend supervises a factory for a fixed salary.
(i) Identify the role of each person. (ii) Distinguish between Mehak and Fatima on three bases.
items.answer: (i) Mehak – intrapreneur; Fatima – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Fatima; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Mehak – intrapreneur; Fatima – entrepreneur; third friend – manager. (ii) Dependence: within the company vs independent owner; funds: company's vs own/borrowed; risk: borne mainly by the company vs fully by Fatima; reward: salary/bonus vs profit (any three).

items.stem: Rohan lost his factory job when the plant closed and started a tea stall to support the family. Is this a push factor or a pull factor? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Push factor. Unemployment forced Rohan into business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Push factor; 2 marks for the justification: Unemployment forced Rohan into business.

items.stem: Explain "Independence" with reference to the entrepreneurial values and attitudes.
items.answer: Independence: Desire to be one's own boss and take decisions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Desire to be one's own boss and take decisions.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Saanvi refuses to accept digital payments even though customers are going to other shops. (a) Which type of entrepreneur is this? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Drone entrepreneur (b) Saanvi refuses to change despite losses.
items.markingKey: (a) Drone entrepreneur, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Saanvi refuses to change despite losses.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "An underlying characteristic, such as knowledge, skill or motive, that leads to effective performance."
items.answer: Competency
items.markingKey: (b) Competency: An underlying characteristic, such as knowledge, skill or motive, that leads to effective performance.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of innovative entrepreneur but not of imitating entrepreneur?
items.answer: Where common: more common in developed and fast-changing industries
items.markingKey: (c) innovative entrepreneur: Where common: more common in developed and fast-changing industries. The other options describe imitating entrepreneur.
options: Approach: copies successful products or methods
Where common: more common in developed and fast-changing industries
Where common: more common in developing economies
